title: Digital Room demo catalog
description: The curated inventory of showable assets. This file is the core asset of the project: retrieval quality depends far more on this metadata than on the model. All content is public and shown to every audience, so there is no tiering; the only content gate is the approved flag.

notes.description: Free text about the state of this catalog file. Not consumed at runtime.

id.description: Stable kebab-case id. Referenced by tours, followUps and stage directives, so never renumber or reuse.

summary.description: One or two sentences describing what the visitor will see. This text is what retrieval matches against, so write it in the visitor's language, not internal shorthand.

type.description: embed is a third-party player in an iframe, currently YouTube. Unlike video, the host page cannot read its playback position, so chapters and talk-track narration do not apply.

approved.description: Cleared for external use. All Digital Room content is public for every audience, so this is the single content gate in the system. An asset with approved:false must never be retrievable at runtime. Set it only through a real review, never as a default, and always alongside reviewedBy and reviewedOn.

products.description: Product or capability names as a customer would recognise them.

depth.description: Lets the agent match depth to the visitor rather than always opening with the overview.

industries.description: Omit when the asset is industry-neutral. Present means it is a strong match for those industries, not that it is restricted to them.

documentType.description: For document assets: NiCE's own content type for the resource, taken from the nice.com/resources listing taxonomy, for example 'Case study' or 'White paper'. Never an inferred value, because it is shown to the visitor as a badge and a guessed badge presents a guess as a fact. Written by tools/build-catalog.mjs from catalog/nice-resources-enriched.json where typeSource is 'site'.

sizeMB.description: File size in megabytes, written by tools/build-catalog.mjs. Informational: it makes the web-delivery problem visible in the catalog itself.

provider.description: Where the asset physically lives, for example sharepoint, vidyard, youtube, local.

watchUrl.description: For embeds: the canonical public page for the asset, used for attribution and as a fallback if the iframe is blocked.

requiresSignedUrl.description: If true the backend mints a short-lived URL at show time. Never put a long-lived private URL in a stage directive.

chapters.description: For video. talkTrack is what the agent says in the chat rail while the chapter plays, and is what makes this guided rather than passive.

prerequisites.description: Asset ids that should ideally be seen first.

followUps.description: Curated next assets. This is the journey graph, and it beats a semantic guess for 'what should I look at next'.

talkingPoints.description: Approved claims the agent may make about this asset. Anything not here should not be asserted.

keywords.description: Synonyms and competitor or legacy terms a visitor might use, to improve recall.

references.description: Public links offered under the agent's reply so a visitor can bookmark something and read more later. Generated from the asset's products by tools/build-catalog.mjs. Every URL must be verified to resolve: a dead link under an agent reply is worse than no link, because the visitor only discovers it is dead after bookmarking it.

goal.description: What the visitor should understand by the end. The agent uses this to stay on track and to close the tour properly.

approved.description: Cleared for external use. A tour is only as approved as its least-approved step, so validate the steps too.

narration.description: What the agent says when entering this step.

checkIn.description: Optional question asked after the step, to keep the visitor engaged and to gather profile signal.
